title: env.sandbox.slice result
description: The instructions one value depended on, newest first — the order the question was asked in, since a reader starts at the value and walks back towards its inputs.

stop.description: Why the run stopped. Every variant is a distinct fact about the code, not a shade of failure.

offset.description: The signed library-vector offset. Naming it against an fd table is the frontend's, because the tables are its configuration.

seed.description: What the slice was asked to explain, as it was resolved.

index.description: The trace row's index, which together with the address is what makes a loop unambiguous.

occurrence.description: How many times this address had already been executed when this row ran, counted from one.

depth.description: How many edges away from the seed this step was first reached.

defines.description: The locations this step defined that the slice depends on, as d0, a5, ccr or [0x00021000].

uses.description: The locations this step read, as far as the model resolves them.

steps_total.description: Defining steps encountered by the bounded walk, including steps refused by the retention cap. This does not count unexplored dependencies.

items.description: Why one chain of the slice ended. `input` is the answer a slice is looking for: the location was never written during the run, so its value is a seeded register, a memory seed, or a byte of the loaded image. `not_executed` is the seed's own answer: the run never executed that instruction that many times, which is a fact about an execution rather than about a byte of memory.

occurrence.description: Which execution of `address` the seed asked about, counted from one. Present on `not_executed`.

executed.description: How many times the run did execute `address`. Present on `not_executed`.

uses_are_a_superset.description: Whether the reported uses are an over-approximation. Always true for a slice that reached anything, and stated rather than implied: a superset presented as a minimum is a different claim. The slice may include a dependency the run did not really have and will not miss one it did.

trace_truncated.description: Whether the run's own trace was capped before the slice walked it. A capped trace bounds what any slice over it can find.
